Lead source: inbound via blog post + quickstart signup. Small mobile-first indie studio building a social mini-game with persistent rooms. Wants hosted API (self-serve) to avoid ops overhead.

Key quotes / highlights: "We need replies felt instant on mobile — players bounce if responses lag." "Moderation is non-negotiable; we need tooling to catch spam and toxic combos without adding latency."

Technical priorities: low p50 latency (target <120ms from us-east), predictable per-token pricing (concern about spikes), simple SDK for Unity, streaming replies for UI feel, server-side content moderation webhook + client-side quick checks.

Security/compliance: public cloud ok, but must have IP allowlist for server keys, audit logs for moderation events, and retention controls to purge test data. SOC2 mention on call but not a hard blocker for SMB.

Conversation summary: Discovery call 2026-03-02 with Aisha + Ravi. Demo of hosted API and streaming. WhistlePop dev lead (Maya R.) did quick integration test on Android: streaming works but p50 ~180ms to their test device (using their test harness). They will run Redwood quickstart and report token usage pattern.

Risks: spike billing during in-game events (lot of short messages). Need guidance on batching/edge caches. Concerned about moderation false positives impacting UX.

Proposed next steps captured in follow-up email: 1) provide test API keys + Unity sample by 2026-03-12 (done), 2) run 48h stress with simulated players and share logs, 3) 30-min follow-up to review results and discuss quota/cost controls.

Staged requests from customer: "Can we get a 30-day trial cap and simple rate-limit dashboard?"

Internal notes: good candidate for hosted_api self-serve conversion; likely SMB ARR if adoption climbs. Provide examples for moderation rules (regex + classifier) and recommend p95 fallback to smaller context for cost control. Keep follow-ups lightweight — prefer email + short calls.
